quiz.dq-14362: There is no unique correct option under the supplied source: options 0 and 3 are suitable. Correct the histogram distractor and solution, which wrongly exclude the booklet’s discrete histograms, and revise the question/options to establish one correct answer.

quiz.dq-14363: This grouped-data exclusion task introduces box plots, which are absent from the supplied teaching and questions, and incorrectly claims that grouped continuous frequencies suffice for stem-and-leaf and box displays. theory: The distribution fact groups dot plots, stem-and-leaf plots and histograms under undifferentiated numerical data. State the booklet’s distinction: dot plots and stem-and-leaf plots display numerical discrete values, while histograms can display discrete or continuous numerical distributions.

findings: practice.foundation[3]: The cited Book 3 question asks students to compare two classes, not select a display for clusters and outliers in one dataset; Book 2 only teaches this display purpose. Replace with a Foundation adaptation of an actual graph-selection question, such as choosing a graph for repeated height measurements over time, and update structure.

practice.development[0]: Replace the absolute claim that a sector graph shows 'not exact frequencies' with the explanation that a sector graph primarily shows proportions and requires the total to recover actual counts. Preserve the question and column-graph answer.

practice.development[2]: Neither cited passage asks students to select a single-dataset display that retains every value; the large-range advantage is theory only. Replace with a Development adaptation of an actual selection-and-justification task, such as choosing a display for spending shares, and update structure.

practice.mastery[1]: The source critiques joining unordered categorical values, not numerical frequencies; combining that critique with another question does not establish this task type. The supplied graph can serve as a frequency polygon, so the asserted poor choice is also unjustified. Replace with a Mastery adaptation asking why a line graph is unsuitable for unordered categories and requesting a better display; update structure.

quiz.q4: The cited source asks for comparison of two classes, not selection of a single-dataset display for spread and outliers. Replace with an adapted booklet graph-selection question under the same id and update structure, options and solution. Avoid the blanket claim that a line graph requires a time series, since the booklet also teaches frequency polygons.
